recipes.name: Grilled Chicken Pineapple Sliders
ingredients_raw: salt and black pepper to taste
3 skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut in half
6 Hawaiian bread rolls - split and toasted

steps.text: Whisk lemon juice, lime juice, cider vinegar, salt, and black pepper together in a large glass or ceramic bowl. Add chicken; toss to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap; marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.

Remove chicken from marinade; shake off excess. Discard remaining marinade. Cook chicken on the preheated grill until juices run clear when pierced with a fork, 5 to 7 minutes per side. Grill pineapple until heated through and grill marks appear, 2 to 3 minutes per side.

Spread 1 teaspoon teriyaki sauce on bottom half of 1 toasted roll; add 1 lettuce leaf, 1 halved chicken breast, 1 pineapple slice, 1 onion slice, and top half roll. Repeat with the remaining teriyaki sauce, rolls, lettuce, chicken, pineapple, and onion.

raw_recipe.headline: Grilled Chicken Pineapple Sliders
raw_recipe.description: This grilled chicken pineapple sliders recipe grills marinated chicken plus pineapple rings, then layers onto Hawaiian rolls with red onion and lettuce.

review.reviewBody: Great recipe! When I made it, I didn't realize how long it was supposed to marinate for. I only let it sit for maybe 30 mins. Still great flavor. I also didnt realize the chicken I had wasn't boneless. I still grilled it but turned it into Shredded Grilled Chicken Pineapple Sliders. Also, instead of spreading the teriyaki sauce onto the bun, I added the 2 Tbsp into the shredded chicken and mixed it. It turned out just as Awesome! Great flavors!

I added fresh chopped garlic and a Tbsp of teriyaki glaze. I also put garlic and onion powder on the chicken before marinating. I let the chicken marinate for about 3 hrs before cooking. I grilled the red onion and made sriracha mayo. The combination of the sweet pineapple and the spicy mayo was fantastic. I left off the lettuce as I didn’t really feel it was needed, however it probably would have given it an additional layer of flavor and some crunch since the onion was cooked. Would definitely make this again.

Ok, I did change it (a bit) but I basically followed the recipe. Love this recipe! Nice change and I will make it often throughout the summer. My changes: I added the teriyaki sauce to the marinade and added an 1/2 tsp of our own homemade spicy pepper blend. (We love spicy) Added grilled jalapeño peppers (from the garden). We also used regular honey slider rolls. Because I didn't drizzle teriyaki sauce on the rolls, I felt it was dry, although the taste was amazing, so we spread a blackened Cajun mustard on each one and OMG! That pushed it right over the top for me. It went from being a really good recipe to an amazing recipe.

Excellent! Grilled the chicken, pineapple and red onions. Did not have teriyaki so used hoisin instead. Used thighs instead of breasts due to personal preference. Sliced everything and ate on romain lettuce leaves to avoid the carbs. Will make again.
I just marinated in teriyaki for 24 hours. Used chicken thighs. Dipped pineapple and onion in teriyaki and grilled. Used mayo in the bread. So good!!

Meh. My hubs and I weren't fond of these. We both agree that the teriyaki sauce should be used as a marinade AND to baste the chicken with (skipping the citrus altogether) rather than as a condiment on each sandwich. A dab of mayo would be a better choice, IMHO. We also felt that the pineapple should be basted with some of the teriyaki as well and that the onion should be grilled rather than raw. Thankfully, I grilled both. Maybe these will float your boat, but they need quite a bit of tweaking to suit us. Thanks anyways, Lindsay-Lou. :)

My whole family loved this. I marinated this overnight and I added garlic, onions, the pineapple juice, soy sauce(instead of Salt) and a circle of teriyaki sauce. It turned out perfect! Chicken was just right! Even my 5 year step-son loved it! Thank you so much for this recipe!
I brushed the chicken with the sauce while grilling.

Family loved it! They said it tasted like they were eating restaurant food. I did grill the onions and toasted the rolls on the BBQ also. Some added Havarti cheese too. I really liked how the marinade did alittle of the cooking. It made the BBQ cook time faster. Will make this again.

made as directed, I placed sliced jalapeno's under the pineapple. Now that gave it the sweet heat that I like. also topped with baby Swiss. 
Thanks for the recipe

SUPERB! It's not a slider, it's a meal! I let my chicken marinate all afternoon and wow, amazing. I also used my home made herb rolls, fresh pineapple, white onion, and spinach leaves instead of lettuce. Amazing pops of flavor with each bite.
So good. I left the onion off (personal preference), but kept the rest as is.
It was just okay...The sour flavor of the chicken overpowered the other flavors. Would not marinate in the lemon in the future for so long (45 min)....maybe not at all. I used chicken tenders.

made these yesterday for a party and they were a big hit everybody to love them. I used chicken tenders and marinated them and teriyaki sauce, a lot of pineapple juice, apple cider vinegar, lemon, lime and a little fresh cracked pepper.
I grilled everything a couple of hours ahead of time and put it into a slow cooker to keep it warm.

Just great. A terrrific go to recipe when company is coming and you just want a little something quick and different. I did fine the Hawaain roles a little small although they go with the theme of the dish. Next time I may use larger roles. Everyone loved it!!
Followed recipe and it was great.
